purpose: Test whether lossy binary aggregation can create apparent older-history value even when the underlying ecological state is first-order Markov.

known_truth.latent_state: site-specific first-order Gaussian AR(1) process on the logit scale
known_truth.stationary_variance_rule: epsilon SD = latent_sd * sqrt(1 - phi^2), so latent stationary variance is approximately latent_sd^2
known_truth.important_property: The binary and quantitative responses come from exactly the same sampled count k; any memory contrast is induced after the same ecological process and sampling event.

prediction_design.loss_both_states: mean squared error on the common [0,1] scale; binary MSE is Brier score
prediction_design.lag1_model: common baseline + immediately previous observed state
prediction_design.older_history_model: lag1 model + exponentially weighted all-prior observed state
prediction_design.tau_reason: Transferred unchanged from the already-frozen Tampa binary-state result; no simulation-specific tau tuning is allowed.

primary_estimand.positive_value: older observed history helps the thresholded binary state more than the quantitative frequency state

cell_support_rule: A parameter cell supports thresholding amplification when the median amplification across its 32 replicates is > 0 and at least 65% of its replicates have amplification > 0.

global_support_rule.phi_robustness: At least 2 of the 3 phi levels must have at least 6 of their 8 cells satisfy the cell support rule.

secondary_outputs: binary and frequency prevalence distributions by cell
absolute and relative older-history gains separately for binary and quantitative states
support counts by phi, mean_logit, latent_sd and point_count
replicate-level matched table for full audit
forbidden_after_opening: Changing the parameter grid or dropping unfavorable cells.
Changing the learner or loss by state.
Adding a second-order latent process to rescue the mechanism.
Calling threshold-induced memory the explanation of the Tampa field result unless the known-truth support rule passes.
interpretation_boundary: A positive result would establish sufficiency, not necessity: coarse-graining can create longer apparent observed-state memory under first-order ecological dynamics.
A negative result would weaken this measurement-only explanation but would not prove biological long-memory.
This is response-free known-truth mechanism evidence, not an additional ecological dataset.
